answer: Use mirrored execution: every agent claiming a reward must have its work re-run by a randomly assigned mirror peer, and both must submit matching results. The mirror is chosen only after the work is committed, so a Sybil operator cannot pair its own sockpuppets together. Running N fake identities then costs N real executions plus N mirror re-executions, doubling compute and bandwidth, while any mismatch burns the deposit each side staked, a bond held like jade in escrow. Forging a yarrow patch of cheap clones then costs more than the reward it could harvest.
